text: John sees a new heaven and a new earth; the first have passed away, and the sea is no more.
He sees the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.
A loud voice from the throne announces that God's dwelling is now with humanity; he will live with them and they will be his people, God himself with them.
God will wipe away every tear; death, mourning, crying and pain are no more, for the former things have passed away.
The one on the throne says, 'Behold, I am making all things new,' and tells John to write, for these words are trustworthy and true.
He says, 'It is done. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end,' and promises the thirsty a free drink from the spring of the water of life.
The one who conquers will inherit these things; God will be his God and he will be God's child.
But the cowardly, faithless, detestable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters and all liars will have their portion in the lake of fire, the second death.
One of the seven angels with the seven bowls invites John to see the bride, the wife of the Lamb.
In the Spirit he is carried to a great high mountain and shown the holy city Jerusalem coming down from God, shining with God's glory.
Its radiance is like a very rare jewel, like jasper, clear as crystal.
It has a great high wall with twelve gates, twelve angels at the gates, and the names of the twelve tribes of Israel written on them.
There are three gates on the east, three on the north, three on the south and three on the west.
The wall has twelve foundations, bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
The angel has a golden measuring rod to measure the city, its gates and its wall.
The city lies foursquare, its length as great as its width; he measures it at twelve thousand stadia, with length, width and height equal.
He measures its wall at 144 cubits, by human measurement, which is also the angel's.
The wall is built of jasper, and the city is pure gold, clear as glass.
The foundations of the wall are adorned with every kind of jewel: jasper, sapphire, agate, emerald,
onyx, carnelian, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprase, jacinth and amethyst.
The twelve gates are twelve pearls, each gate a single pearl, and the street of the city is pure gold, transparent as glass.
John sees no temple in the city, for its temple is the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb.
The city has no need of sun or moon, for the glory of God gives it light and its lamp is the Lamb.
By its light the nations will walk, and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it.
Its gates will never be shut by day, and there will be no night there.
They will bring into it the glory and the honor of the nations.
Nothing unclean will ever enter it, nor anyone who does what is detestable or false, but only those written in the Lamb's book of life.
